description: Wire shape of the config-resolve 200 body: `{ "values": {key: string|null}, "secretKeys": [string] }` (bd:envpit-durd, AC-SEC-E11). `body` is the raw decoded JSON the transport received; `expected` is either `{"values": ..., "secretKeys": [...]}` (the unwrapped snapshot the client goes on to serve) or `{"expectedError": "NetworkError"}` — the SAME class error-mapping.json's `invalid-json-body` case uses, because a body that parses as JSON but is not this envelope is a malformed response, not a distinct new failure mode. Ground truth: envpit (main repo) apps/api/src/config-management/config-resolve.controller.ts (both `ApiKeyConfigResolveController` and the key-scope-inferred `ApiKeyScopedConfigResolveController` return the identical shape) + config.service.ts `resolveEnvironmentSecretsInternal`.

notes.breakingChange: Before bd:envpit-durd the same route returned a BARE `{key: value}` map with no secret labelling at all. That shape is deliberately REJECTED here rather than accepted as a legacy fallback: a bare map silently means `secretKeys = []`, which every native-env-merge path (see env-merge.json) would read as 'this environment has no secrets' and merge production secrets into the process environment while reporting that it excluded them. Failing loudly against a pre-durd server is the safe direction. There were zero published SDK releases when this landed, so no real consumer is broken by the strictness.
notes.secretKeysIsNamesOnly: `secretKeys` NEVER carries a value — only the names of `is_secret=true` keys. The flag is key-level, not value-level, so a secret key whose value is unset in this environment still appears in `secretKeys` while its `values` entry is `null` (`unset-secret-is-still-listed` below).
notes.javaErrorName: Java's taxonomy names this class `NetworkException`; the mapping is the one already established by error-mapping.json, not a new one.

cases.name: secret-key-absent-from-values-is-tolerated
cases.why: Not an error: the two lists are built from the same query server-side, but a client that hard-failed on a name it could not cross-reference would turn any future server-side widening of `secretKeys` into an outage. An unmatched name simply excludes nothing.

cases.name: legacy-bare-map-is-rejected
cases.why: The pre-durd shape. See notes.breakingChange — accepting it would mean merging secrets while reporting none were found.

cases.name: legacy-empty-map-is-rejected-too
cases.why: `{}` is ambiguous between 'pre-durd server, empty environment' and 'new server that dropped both fields'. Rejecting it keeps the envelope check total — there is no body that is valid only by accident.

cases.name: secret-keys-not-an-array-is-rejected
cases.why: A bare string is iterable character-by-character in several of these languages — accepted, it would produce a secretKeys set of single letters that matches nothing.

cases.name: non-string-value-inside-values-is-rejected
cases.why: Unchanged from the pre-durd contract — every config value crosses the wire as a JSON string or null. This case only re-asserts that the check moved INSIDE `values` rather than being dropped during the unwrap.

cases.name: unknown-extra-envelope-field-is-ignored
cases.why: Forward compatibility: the envelope may grow. Only `values` and `secretKeys` are load-bearing.
